parent_act_name: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
title_english: Power of the Committee or the Board to amend its own orders
summary_or_content: Without prejudice to the provisions for appeal and revision contained in this Act, the Committee or the Board may, on an application received in this behalf, amend any orders passed by itself, as to the institution to which a child is to be sent or as to the person under whose care or supervision a child is to be placed under this Act: Provided that during the course of hearing for amending any such orders, there shall be at least two members of the Board of which one shall be the Principal Magistrate and at least three members of the Committee and all persons concerned, or their authorised representatives, whose views shall be heard by the Committee or the Board, as the case may be, before the said orders are amended. Clerical mistakes in orders passed by the Committee or the Board or errors arising therein from any accidental slip or omission may, at any time, be corrected by the Committee or the Board, as the case may be, either on its own motion or on an application received in this behalf.
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
summary_or_content: The State Government may create a fund in such name as it thinks fit for the welfare and rehabilitation of the children dealt with under this Act. There shall be credited to the fund such voluntary donations, contributions or subscriptions as may be made by any individual or organisation. The fund created under sub-section (1) shall be administered by the Department of the State Government implementing this Act in such manner and for such purposes as may be prescribed.
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
title_english: State Child Protection Society and District Child Protection Unit
summary_or_content: Every State Government shall constitute a Child Protection Society for the State and Child Protection Unit for every District, consisting of such officers and other employees as may be appointed by that Government, to take up matters relating to children with a view to ensure the implementation of this Act, including the establishment and maintenance of institutions under this Act, notification of competent authorities in relation to the children and their rehabilitation and co-ordination with various official and non-official agencies concerned and to discharge such other functions as may be prescribed.
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
title_english: Child Welfare Police Officer and Special Juvenile Police Unit
summary_or_content: In every police station, at least one officer, not below the rank of assistant sub-inspector, with aptitude, appropriate training and orientation may be designated as the child welfare police officer to exclusively deal with children either as victims or perpetrators, in co-ordination with the police, voluntary and non-governmental organisations. To co-ordinate all functions of police related to children, the State Government shall constitute Special Juvenile Police Units in each district and city, headed by a police officer not below the rank of a Deputy Superintendent of Police or above and consisting of all police officers designated under sub-section (1) and two social workers having experience of working in the field of child welfare, of whom one shall be a woman. All police officers of the Special Juvenile Police Units shall be provided special training, especially at induction as child welfare police officer, to enable them to perform their functions more effectively. Special Juvenile Police Unit also includes Railway police dealing with children.
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
title_english: Public awareness on provisions of Act
summary_or_content: The Central Government and every State Government, shall take necessary measures to ensure that– the provisions of this Act are given wide publicity through media including television, radio and print media at regular intervals so as to make the general public, children and their parents or guardians aware of such provisions; the officers of the Central Government, State Government and other concerned, persons are imparted periodic training on the matters relating to the implementation of the provisions of this Act.
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
summary_or_content: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights constituted under section 3, or as the case may be, the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights constituted under section 17 (herein referred to as the National Commission or the State Commission, as the case may be), of the Commissions for Protection of Child rights Act, 2005 (4 of 2006), shall, in addition to the functions assigned to them under the said Act, also monitor the implementation of the provisions of this Act, in such manner, as may be prescribed. The National Commission or, as the case may be, the State Commission, shall, while inquiring into any matter relating to any offence under this Act, have the same powers as are vested in the National Commission or the State Commission under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 (4 of 2006). The National Commission or, as the case may be, the State Commission, shall also include its activities under this section, in the annual report referred to in section 16 of the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 (4 of 2006).
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
summary_or_content: The State Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act: Provided that the Central Government may, frame model rules in respect of all or any of the matters with respect to which the State Government is required to make rules and where any such model rules have been framed in respect of any such matter, they shall apply to the State mutatis mutandis until the rules in respect of that matter are made by the State Government and while making any such rules, they conform to such model rules. In particular, and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers, such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely:– manner of inquiry in case of a missing or run away child or whose parents cannot be found under sub-clause (vii) of clause (14) of section 2; responsibilities of the Child Welfare Officer attached to a Children's Home under clause (18) of section 2; qualifications of the members of the Board under sub-section (2) of section 4; induction training and sensitisation of all members of the Board under sub-section (5) of section 4; term of office of the members of the Board and the manner in which such member may resign under sub-section (6) of section 4; time of the meetings of the Board and the rules of procedure in regard to the transaction of business at its meeting under sub-section (1) of section 7; qualifications, experience and payment of fees of an interpreter or translator under clause (d) of sub-section (3) of section 8; any other function of the Board under clause (n) of sub-section (3) of section 8; persons through whom any child alleged to be in conflict with law may be produced before the Board and the manner in which such a child may be sent to an observation home or place of safety under sub-section (2) of section 10; manner in which a person apprehended and not released on bail by the officer-in-charge of the police station may be kept in an observation home until such person is brought before a Board under sub-section (2) of section 12; format for information on pendency in the Board to the Chief Judicial Magistrate or the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and District Magistrate on quarterly basis under sub-section (3) of section 16; monitoring procedures and list of monitoring authorities under sub-section (2) of section 20; manner in which the relevant records of the child may be destroyed by the Board, police or the court under sub-section (2) of section 24; qualifications of the members of the Child Welfare Committee under subsection (5) of section 27; rules and procedures with regard to transaction of business at the meetings of the Child Welfare Committee under sub-section (1) of section 28; process of restoration of abandoned or lost children to their families under clause (x) of section 30; manner of submitting the report to the Committee and the manner of sending and entrusting the child to Children's Home or fit facility or fit person under sub-section (2) of section 31; manner of holding an inquiry by the Child Welfare Committee under subsection (1) of section 36; manner in which a child may be sent to a Specialised Adoption Agency if the child is below six years of age, Children's Home or to a fit facility or person or foster family, till suitable means of rehabilitation are found for the child including manner in which situation of the child placed in a Children's Home or with a fit facility or person or foster family, may be reviewed by the Committee under sub-section (3) of section 36; manner in which a quarterly report may be submitted by the Committee to the District Magistrate for review of pendency of cases under sub-section (4) of section 36; any other order related to any other function of the Committee under clause (iii) of sub-section (2) of section 37; information to be given every month by the Committee to State Agency and Authority regarding number of children declared legally free for adoption and number of cases pending under sub-section (5) of section 38; manner in which all institutions under this Act shall be registered under sub-section (1) of section 41; procedure for cancelling or withholding registration of an institution that fails to provide rehabilitation and re-integration services under sub-section (7) of section 41; manner in which information shall be sent every month by the open shelter to the District Child Protection Unit and Committee under sub-section (3) of section 43; procedure for placing children in foster care including group foster care under sub-section (1) of section 44; procedure for inspection of children in foster care under sub-section (4) of section 44; manner in which foster family shall provide education, health and nutrition to the child under sub-section (6) of section 44; procedure and criteria in which foster care services shall be provided to children under sub-section (7) of section 44; format for inspection of foster families by the Committee to check the well being of children under sub-section (8) of section 44; purpose of undertaking various programmes of sponsorship of children, such as individual to individual sponsorship, group sponsorship or community sponsorship under sub-section (1) of section 45; duration of sponsorship under sub-section (3) of section 45; manner of providing financial support to any child leaving institutional care on completing eighteen years of age under section 46; management and monitoring of observation homes, including the standards and various types of services to be provided by them for rehabilitation and social integration of a child alleged to be in conflict with law and the circumstances under which, and the manner in which, the registration of an observation home may be granted or withdrawn under sub-section (3) of section 47; management and monitoring of special homes including the standards and various types of services to be provided to them under sub-section (2) and sub-section (3) of section 48; monitoring and management of children's homes including the standards and the nature of services to be provided by them, based on individual care plans for each child under sub-section (3) of section 50; manner in which a Board or the Committee shall recognise, a facility being run by a Governmental organisation or a voluntary or non-governmental organisation registered under any law for the time being in force, fit to temporarily take the responsibility of a child for a specific purpose after due inquiry regarding the suitability of the facility and the organisation to take care of the child under sub-section (1) of section 51; procedure of verification of credentials, for recognising any person fit to temporarily receive a child for care, protection and treatment of such child for a specified period by the Board or the Committee under sub-section (1) of section 52; manner in which services shall be provided by an institution under this Act for rehabilitation and re-integration of children and standards for basic requirements such as food, shelter, clothing and medical attention under sub-section (1) of section 53; manner in which Management Committee shall be set up by each institution for management of the institution and monitoring of the progress of every child under sub-section (2) of section 53; activities that may be taken up by children's committees under sub-section (3) of section 53; appointment of inspection committees for all institutions registered or recognised fit, for the State and district under sub-section (1) of section 54; manner in which Central Government or State Government may independently evaluate the functioning of the Board, Committee, special juvenile police units, registered institutions, or recognised fit facilities and persons, including the period and through persons or institutions under sub-section (1) of section 55; manner in which institutions shall furnish details of children declared legally free for adoption to the Specialised Adoption Agency under sub-section (2) of section 66; any other function of the Authority under clause (e) of section 68; criteria for the selection or nomination of the Members of the Steering Committee of the Authority and their tenure as well as the terms and conditions of their appointment under sub-section (2) of section 69; manner in which Steering Committee of the Authority shall meet under sub-section (4) of section 69; manner in which the Authority shall submit an annual report to the Central Government under sub-section (1) of section 71; functions of the Authority under sub-section (2) of section 72; manner in which the Authority shall maintain proper accounts and other relevant records and prepare an annual statement of accounts under sub-section (1) of section 73; period that the Committee or Board may think necessary for the treatment of children who are found to be suffering from a disease requiring prolonged medical treatment or physical or mental complaint that will respond to treatment to a fit facility under section 92; procedure for transfer of child under sub-section (1) of section 95; provision for travelling allowance to the escorting staff for the child under sub-section (3) of section 95; procedure to be followed by the Committee or a Board while holding any inquiry, appeal or revision under sub-section (1) of section 103; manner in which juvenile justice fund shall be administered under sub-section (3) of section 105; functioning of the Child Protection Society for the State and Child Protection Units for every district under section 106; to enable the National Commission, or as the case may be, the State Commission to monitor implementation of the provisions of this Act under sub-section (1) of section 109; any other matter which is required to be, or may be, prescribed. Every rule and every regulation made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in session, for a total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one session or in two or more successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session immediately following the session or the successive sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any modification in the rule or regulation or both Houses agree that the rule or regulation should not be made, the rule or regulation shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so, however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule or regulation. Every rule made by the State Government under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the State Legislature.
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
summary_or_content: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 (56 of 2000) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Acts shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
summary_or_content: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government may, by order, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, remove the difficulty: Provided that no such order shall be made after the expiry of the period of two years from the commencement of this Act. However, order made under this section shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament.
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
title_english: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
summary_or_content: An Act to provide protection against sexual harassment of women at workplace and for prevention and redressal of complaints.
source_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

parent_act_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
summary_or_content: # The Sexual Harassment Of Women At The Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 **ACT NO. 14 OF 2013** *[22nd April, 2013]* An Act to provide protection against sexual harassment of women at workplace and for the prevention and redressal of complaints of sexual harassment and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS sexual harassment results in violation of the fundamental rights of a woman to equality under articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution of India and her right to life and to live with dignity under article 21 of the Constitution and right to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade or business with includes a right to a safe environment free from sexual harassment; AND WHEREAS the protection against sexual harassment and the right to work with dignity are universally recognised human rights by international conventions and instruments such as Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women, which has been ratified on the 25th June, 1993 by the Government of India; AND WHEREAS it is expedient to make provisions for giving effect to the said Convention for protection of women against sexual harassment at workplace. parent_act_name: Constitution of India, 1950
title_english: Right to Life, Dignity & Personal Liberty
summary_or_content: Guaranteed under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, no citizen or person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
legal_remedy: Direct constitutional Writ Petition (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Quo Warranto, Certiorari) under Article 32 or 226.
source_authority: LegalConnect Constitutional Review Directorate

parent_act_name: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023
section_or_code: Section 35, Section 47, Section 48, Section 50, Section 51, Section 58
summary_or_content: Codified procedural safeguards governing police detainment and arrest under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS 2023), establishing strict accountability for law enforcement.
legal_remedy: Regular or Anticipatory Bail before the Judicial Magistrate or Sessions Court under BNSS Section 480 / 482; Habeas Corpus for illegal custody beyond 24 hours.
source_authority: LegalConnect Criminal Procedural Directorate

parent_act_name: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 & Central Motor Vehicles Rules
title_english: Traffic Police Checks, DigiLocker & Challan Safeguards
summary_or_content: Statutory protections governing vehicular inspections, digital document validation, on-the-spot compounding, and protection against unauthorized key confiscation.
legal_remedy: Contest challan before the Virtual Court / Metropolitan Magistrate Traffic Court; file complaint on National Grievance Portal CPGRAMS or State Traffic Vigilance.
source_authority: LegalConnect Transport Legal Desk

parent_act_name: RBI Master Circular on Customer Protection & Information Technology Act
section_or_code: Circular DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18, IT Act Section 43A, IT Act Section 46
title_english: Zero Customer Liability in Cyber Banking & UPI Fraud
summary_or_content: RBI mandated insulation protecting account holders from financial losses caused by unauthorized electronic banking, ATM cloning, SIM-swap, and UPI breaches.
legal_remedy: Complaint before the RBI Banking Ombudsman; petition before the State IT Adjudicating Officer under IT Act Section 46.
source_authority: LegalConnect Banking & Fintech Legal Council

parent_act_name: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 & E-Commerce Rules, 2020
section_or_code: Section 2(9), Section 35, Section 38, Section 84, Rule 5 E-Commerce Rules
title_english: Consumer Rights, E-Commerce Refunds & Defective Goods
summary_or_content: Comprehensive statutory protections shielding consumers from defective products, deceptive advertisements, unauthorized cancellation fees, and unfair trade practices.
legal_remedy: Filing of complaint before District Consumer Commission (claims up to ₹50 Lakh) or State Commission (₹50 Lakh to ₹2 Crore) under Section 35.
source_authority: LegalConnect Consumer Redressal Council

parent_act_name: Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 & NHRC Patient Rights Charter
section_or_code: Section 12(2) CEA, NHRC Charter Article 1 to 17, Article 21 Constitution
title_english: Emergency Patient Care & Hospital Charter of Rights
summary_or_content: Binding statutory rights ensuring emergency medical stabilization without upfront payment, access to medical records within 72 hours, and protection against corpse detention.
legal_remedy: Emergency writ petition in High Court under Article 226; complaint before State Medical Council; claim before Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
source_authority: LegalConnect Medico-Legal Advisory Board

parent_act_name: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 & Model Tenancy Act
section_or_code: Section 106 TPA, Section 108 TPA, Model Tenancy Act Provisions
title_english: Tenant Rights Against Unlawful Eviction & Utility Cutoff
summary_or_content: Statutory safeguards protecting residential tenants from coercive lockouts, sudden utility disconnection, arbitrary rent increases, and privacy invasions.
legal_remedy: Suit for Permanent Injunction against unlawful dispossession; petition before the Rent Court for mandatory restoration of essential utilities.
source_authority: LegalConnect Real Estate & Tenancy Division

parent_act_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
section_or_code: Section 12, Section 17, Section 18, Section 19, Section 20, Section 22
summary_or_content: Comprehensive legal protections for women against physical abuse, emotional cruelty, financial deprivation, and sexual violence in domestic relationships.
legal_remedy: Filing petition under Section 12 PWDVA before the Judicial Magistrate First Class or Metropolitan Magistrate.
source_authority: LegalConnect Family Law Directorate

parent_act_name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
title_english: Citizen Data Privacy & Digital Rights (DPDP Act)
summary_or_content: Codifies statutory control for Indian citizens over their personal data processed by technology corporations, banks, and digital intermediaries under DPDP Act 2023.
legal_remedy: Formal complaint before the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI) and appellate remedies before TDSAT.
emergency_helpline: Data Protection Board of India Desk: 1800-LC-DPDP
source_authority: LegalConnect Digital Technology Council

parent_act_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
summary_or_content: Binding statutory framework ensuring a safe workplace for women, mandating Internal Complaints Committees (ICC), confidentiality, and protection from employer retaliation.
legal_remedy: Inquiry before the Internal Committee (IC) / Local Committee (LC); appeal before the Appellate Authority under industrial employment rules or High Court.
source_authority: LegalConnect Labour & Employment Division

parent_act_name: DGCA Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) Section 3, Series M, Part IV
section_or_code: Clause 3.3 Delay Remedies, Clause 3.4 Cancellation Compensation, Clause 3.5 Denied Boarding
title_english: Air Passenger Rights for Flight Delays, Cancellations & Baggage
summary_or_content: Binding statutory protections under the DGCA Passenger Charter guaranteeing compensation, free meals, alternative flights, and refunds for airline defaults.
legal_remedy: Grievance through DGCA AirSewa portal; complaint before the District Consumer Commission for deficiency in service and mental harassment.
source_authority: LegalConnect Consumer & Aviation Desk

parent_act_name: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
title_english: Homebuyer Rights Against Possession Delays (RERA Act)
summary_or_content: Statutory protections under RERA 2016 empowering allottees to claim monthly interest for delayed possession, full refunds with interest, and 5-year defect warranties.
legal_remedy: Complaint under Section 31 before the State Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA); claim before Adjudicating Officer for compensation.
source_authority: LegalConnect Real Estate Regulatory Council

parent_act_name: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
title_english: Senior Citizen Maintenance & Property Gift Deed Revocation
summary_or_content: Protects the dignity, health, and property of elderly parents, empowering SDM Maintenance Tribunals to void abusive property transfers and enforce maintenance.
legal_remedy: Application for Maintenance and Revocation of Property Deeds before the Maintenance Tribunal (SDM Office).
source_authority: LegalConnect Elderly Rights Advisory

parent_act_name: Code on Wages, 2019 & Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017
section_or_code: Section 3 Code on Wages, Section 5 Maternity Benefit Act, Section 11 Creche Facility, Section 12 Dismissal Ban
summary_or_content: Guarantees equal wages for equal work without gender discrimination and secures 26 weeks of paid maternity leave with complete job security for working women.
legal_remedy: Complaint before the Labor Commissioner / Inspector under Section 17 of the Maternity Benefit Act.
source_authority: LegalConnect Labor & Employment Division

parent_act_name: Right to Information Act, 2005
title_english: Right to Information & Public Accountability (RTI Act)
summary_or_content: Empowers any citizen to inspect public records, examine infrastructure works, and secure certified copies of government files within strict statutory timelines.
legal_remedy: First Appeal under Section 19(1) and Second Appeal before the Central/State Information Commission under Section 19(3).
source_authority: LegalConnect Administrative Law Directorate

parent_act_name: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
summary_or_content: Statutory guarantees ensuring non-discrimination, 4% job reservation, accessible public infrastructure, and legal capacity for persons with disabilities.
legal_remedy: Complaint before the Chief Commissioner or State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities under Section 75 / 80; writ petition in High Court.
source_authority: LegalConnect Accessibility & Human Rights Directorate

parent_act_name: POCSO Act, 2012 & Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
section_or_code: Section 19 POCSO, Section 24 POCSO, Section 33 POCSO, Section 75 JJ Act
title_english: Child Safeguards & Abuse Protection (POCSO & JJ Act)
summary_or_content: Stringent statutory safeguards shielding minors from sexual offenses, cruelty, and child labor, with child-friendly court procedures and mandatory reporting.
legal_remedy: Cognizance before the Special POCSO Court; Child Welfare Committee (CWC) orders under Juvenile Justice Act.
source_authority: LegalConnect Child Safeguards Directorate

parent_act_name: Mental Healthcare Act, 2017
title_english: Mental Health Patient Autonomy & Advance Directives
summary_or_content: Guarantees the dignity, confidentiality, and autonomy of persons with mental illness, decriminalizes suicide attempts, and introduces binding Advance Directives.
legal_remedy: Complaint before the Mental Health Review Board; appeal before the High Court; complaint to Insurance Ombudsman.
source_authority: LegalConnect Healthcare Law Council

parent_act_name: Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014
summary_or_content: Protects street vendors and informal traders from arbitrary harassment and unlawful confiscation, guaranteeing town vending surveys and 30-day eviction notices.
legal_remedy: Grievance before the Street Vendors Dispute Redressal Committee under Section 20; writ petition in High Court.
source_authority: LegalConnect Informal Labor Rights Desk

parent_act_name: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
section_or_code: Article 21A Constitution, Section 3 RTE, Section 12(1)(c), Section 16, Section 17
title_english: Free & Compulsory Education Rights (RTE Act & Art 21A)
summary_or_content: Constitutional guarantee under Article 21A securing free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14, with a mandatory 25% quota in private unaided schools.
legal_remedy: Complaint before the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR) / NCPCR; writ petition under Article 226 in High Court.
source_authority: LegalConnect Constitutional & Education Council

parent_act_name: Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019
summary_or_content: Secures the fundamental right of transgender persons to self-perceived gender identity without medical procedures, guaranteeing non-discrimination across all spheres.
legal_remedy: Grievance before the District Magistrate / Complaint Officer; petition before the National/State Human Rights Commission; Article 226 High Court writ.
source_authority: LegalConnect Civil Liberties Directorate

parent_act_name: National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 & Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
section_or_code: Article 21 Constitution, Section 14 NGT, Section 15 NGT, Section 19 NGT
title_english: Right to Clean Environment, Air & Water (NGT Act & Art 21)
summary_or_content: Recognizes the right to pollution-free air and water as an integral facet of Article 21, empowering citizens to approach the National Green Tribunal directly.
legal_remedy: Original Application under Section 14/15 before the National Green Tribunal; writ petition in High Court under Article 226.
source_authority: LegalConnect Environmental Law Division

parent_act_name: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 & BNSS 2023
section_or_code: Article 39A Constitution, Section 12 LSAA, Section 479 BNSS 2023, Section 340 BNSS
title_english: Undertrial Bail Rights & Mandatory Free Legal Aid (Art 39A)
summary_or_content: Codifies the constitutional right to free legal representation under Article 39A and maximum statutory custody limits ensuring undertrials are released on personal bond.
legal_remedy: Bail application under BNSS Section 479 / 480; Habeas Corpus before the High Court; intervention through the District Legal Services Authority.
source_authority: LegalConnect Legal Aid & Human Rights Cell

parent_act_name: Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 & Central Vigilance Commission Act
section_or_code: Section 4 WBPA, Section 11 WBPA, Section 12 WBPA, PIDPI Resolution
summary_or_content: Safeguards citizens and public servants who expose corruption, misuse of power, or criminal offenses from administrative victimization and physical threats.
legal_remedy: Petition before the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) under PIDPI; writ petition in High Court under Article 226 for protective orders.
source_authority: LegalConnect Governance & Anti-Corruption Bureau

parent_act_name: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (RFCTLARR)
section_or_code: Section 4, Section 16, Section 26, Section 30, Section 31, Section 64
title_english: Fair Land Acquisition Compensation & Resettlement Rights
summary_or_content: Guarantees landowners and affected families up to 4x market value compensation, mandatory Social Impact Assessments, and statutory rehabilitation.
legal_remedy: Reference before the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority (LARR Authority) under Section 64; appeal before the High Court.
source_authority: LegalConnect Property & Land Acquisition Council

parent_act_name: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 & State Police Towing Regulations
title_english: Right Against Vehicle Towing with Passenger Inside
title_hindi: यात्री के अंदर रहते हुए वाहन टो (क्रेन से उठाने) के खिलाफ अधिकार
summary_or_content: Traffic authorities are legally forbidden from towing or hoisting any motor vehicle while the driver or passengers are sitting inside. Towing can only commence after safe evacuation and issuing a formal physical or e-challan receipt.
confrontation_script_en: Officer, under Traffic Police Towing Regulations and Section 127 of the Motor Vehicles Act, you cannot hoist or tow this vehicle while I am inside. Please issue an e-challan for the parking violation and I will move the vehicle immediately.
confrontation_script_hi: अधिकारी महोदय, मोटर वाहन अधिनियम की धारा 127 और ट्रैफिक पुलिस नियमों के तहत जब तक मैं अंदर बैठा हूँ, आप वाहन को क्रेन से नहीं उठा सकते। कृपया पार्किंग उल्लंघन का ई-चालान दें, मैं गाड़ी तुरंत हटा रहा हूँ।
actionable_dos: Remain seated calmly and turn on hazard parking lights.; Request an immediate on-the-spot e-challan without tow fees.; Note the crane registration number and traffic police zone batch.
actionable_donts: Do NOT engage in physical scuffles with tow contractors.; Do NOT step out of the car until the crane drops the cable hoist.; Do NOT pay cash fines without an automated official SMS / printed e-challan.
legal_remedy: Grievance before the Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic), State Human Rights Commission, or Lok Adalat for endangerment under Section 279/336 IPC / BNS Section 106/281.
source_authority: LegalConnect Traffic & Motor Vehicle Directorate

parent_act_name: Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 & Information Technology Act, 2000
section_or_code: Rule 139 CMVR, Section 4 IT Act 2000, Section 139 MVA
title_english: Mandatory Acceptance of DigiLocker & mParivahan Electronic Documents
title_hindi: डिजिलॉकर और एम-परिवहन डिजिटल ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस व आरसी की कानूनी मान्यता
summary_or_content: Digital driving licenses, registration certificates (RC), insurance, and PUC stored in DigiLocker or mParivahan are legally equivalent to original physical documents. Police cannot penalize or demand physical cards.
confrontation_script_en: Officer, under Rule 139 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules and MoRTH Notification RT-11036/64/2017, documents on DigiLocker and mParivahan have statutory equivalence under Section 4 of the IT Act. You are legally required to accept this QR-verified digital license.
confrontation_script_hi: अधिकारी महोदय, केंद्रीय मोटर वाहन नियम 139 और सड़क परिवहन मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना के अनुसार डिजिलॉकर में उपलब्ध ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस और आरसी कानूनी रूप से मान्य हैं। आप इसे अस्वीकार नहीं कर सकते।
actionable_dos: Keep your DigiLocker and mParivahan apps updated and offline-cached before driving.; Show the active government app directly, not a third-party gallery screenshot.; Ensure the QR code is clearly visible and scannable.
actionable_donts: Do NOT show raw gallery screenshots or unauthorized third-party wallet PDFs.; Do NOT hand over your unlocked phone; simply hold it up for the officer to inspect or scan.; Do NOT accept an offline paper challan for "failure to produce documents".
legal_remedy: Grievance before the Superintendent of Police (Traffic) or dismissal of challan in the District Virtual Traffic Court.
source_authority: LegalConnect Digital Mobility Council

parent_act_name: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019
title_english: Breathalyzer Test Protocol & Fresh Disposable Nozzle Rights
title_hindi: ब्रीथ एनालाइज़र (शराब जांच) परीक्षण नियम व नया सीलबंद नोज़ल मांगने का अधिकार
summary_or_content: Citizens subjected to a suspected drink-and-drive inspection have the strict legal right to inspect the breathalyzer, demand a sealed single-use disposable plastic straw opened in front of them, and receive a printed or digital BAC slip. Readings below 30mg per 100ml blood are non-cognizable.
confrontation_script_en: Officer, under Section 203 of the Motor Vehicles Act, I consent to the breath test, but you must open a sealed, sterile disposable nozzle in front of me and provide the machine reading slip.
confrontation_script_hi: अधिकारी महोदय, मोटर वाहन अधिनियम की धारा 203 के तहत मैं श्वास परीक्षण के लिए तैयार हूँ, लेकिन आपको मेरे सामने एक नया सीलबंद प्लास्टिक नोज़ल खोलना होगा और मशीन की प्रिंटेड पर्ची देनी होगी।
actionable_dos: Comply politely with the test request; refusal can result in detention for medical exam under Sec 203(3).; Verify that the sealed packet is opened in front of you.; Demand to see the digital reading and preserve the printed ticket.
actionable_donts: Do NOT put your mouth on an already mounted or open pipe.; Do NOT physically resist officers; instead, demand a hospital blood test.; Do NOT flee a checkpoint, as it creates an adverse legal presumption.
legal_remedy: Contest the challan before the Metropolitan / Judicial Magistrate Court by presenting negative blood test results.
source_authority: LegalConnect Traffic & Motor Vehicle Directorate

parent_act_name: Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010 & Article 21
section_or_code: Section 12(2) CEA, Article 21 Constitution, Section 134 MVA
title_english: Mandatory Emergency Stabilization Without Advance Deposit
title_hindi: अस्पतालों द्वारा अग्रिम भुगतान के बिना अनिवार्य आपातकालीन प्राथमिक उपचार का अधिकार
summary_or_content: Both government and private hospitals are legally mandated to immediately provide first-aid, resuscitation, and emergency stabilization to any critical or trauma victim without demanding advance money, police FIR formalities, or insurance approvals first.
confrontation_script_en: Doctor/Admin, under the Supreme Court landmark ruling in Parmanand Katara and Section 12 of the Clinical Establishments Act, you cannot withhold emergency life-saving stabilization for advance payment or police formalities. You must start treatment immediately.
confrontation_script_hi: डॉक्टर और अस्पताल प्रशासन, सुप्रीम कोर्ट के परमानंद कटारा फैसले और क्लिनिकल प्रतिष्ठान कानून के तहत आप अग्रिम भुगतान या पुलिस औपचारिकताओं के लिए आपातकालीन उपचार नहीं रोक सकते। कृपया तुरंत इलाज शुरू करें।
actionable_dos: Prioritize getting the patient onto a stretcher and into the ICU/casualty ward.; Cite the Parmanand Katara judgment to hospital billing staff.; Keep a record of the refusal if hospital staff causes unreasonable delays.
actionable_donts: Do NOT waste precious golden-hour minutes arguing at the billing counter.; Do NOT allow the hospital to transfer an unstable, critical patient without life support.; Do NOT let hospital staff compel good samaritans to sign admission liability forms.
legal_remedy: Complaint before the State Clinical Establishments Authority, National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), and writ petition under Article 226 for medical negligence.
source_authority: LegalConnect Medico-Legal Council

parent_act_name: Charter of Patient Rights (NHRC/MoHFW) & Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
section_or_code: Section 127 BNS (Old Sec 342 IPC), Section 308 BNS (Extortion), Article 21 Constitution
title_english: Absolute Prohibition Against Detaining Patients or Deceased Bodies for Unpaid Bills
title_hindi: अस्पतालों द्वारा बकाया बिल के लिए शव या मरीज को बंधक बनाने पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध
summary_or_content: Hospitals have zero statutory authority to hold a patient captive or refuse release of a deceased human body over pending financial invoices. Doing so constitutes wrongful confinement and criminal extortion under the law.
confrontation_script_en: Hospital Administration, detaining a deceased body or discharged patient for unpaid bills is illegal confinement under Section 127 of BNS and violates the Supreme Court patient charter. Release the body immediately; financial disputes must be pursued in civil courts, not through detention.
confrontation_script_hi: अस्पताल प्रशासन, बकाया बिल के लिए किसी मृत शरीर या मरीज को रोकना बीएनएस की धारा 127 के तहत गैरकानूनी बंधक और अपराध है। शव को तुरंत परिजनों को सौंपें; वित्तीय विवाद के लिए अदालत जाएं, शव को बंधक नहीं बना सकते।
actionable_dos: Demand immediate release of death certificate and custody of the body in writing.; Call local police to the hospital reception to enforce patient charter compliance.; Offer a signed written dispute letter without surrendering custody rights.
actionable_donts: Do NOT accept that hospitals possess any "lien" or property rights over human remains.; Do NOT sign blank high-interest promissory notes under coercive emotional duress.; Do NOT leave without obtaining an official itemized medical billing breakdown.
legal_remedy: Filing of FIR under Section 127/308 BNS for wrongful confinement and extortion; emergency Habeas Corpus petition before the High Court.
source_authority: LegalConnect Medico-Legal Council

parent_act_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act)
title_english: Mandatory Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) & Workplace Anti-Harassment Safeguards
title_hindi: कार्यस्थल पर आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) का अनिवार्य गठन और पॉश कानून के तहत सुरक्षा
summary_or_content: Every workplace with 10 or more employees must mandatorily constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) presided over by a senior woman employee and an external NGO member. Failure incurs a ₹50,000 fine and cancellation of business license.
confrontation_script_en: Management / HR, under Section 4 of the POSH Act 2013, our organization is legally required to have an active Internal Complaints Committee with an independent external member. A formal complaint under Section 9 must be investigated within 90 days with complete identity protection.
confrontation_script_hi: प्रबंधन / एचआर, पॉश अधिनियम 2013 की धारा 4 के अनुसार हमारे संस्थान में एक स्वतंत्र बाहरी सदस्य वाली आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) होना अनिवार्य है। मेरी शिकायत की 90 दिनों में निष्पक्ष और गोपनीय जांच की जाए।
actionable_dos: Document all incidents with date, time, location, and specific words or actions.; Submit your complaint to the ICC in writing within 3 months of the last incident.; Seek interim relief under Section 12 if you feel threatened or unsafe.
actionable_donts: Do NOT accept informal verbal settlements without written documentation.; Do NOT disclose the proceedings to social media, as Sec 16 mandates strict privacy.; Do NOT tolerate retaliatory poor appraisals or workplace isolation.
legal_remedy: Statutory appeal under Section 18 of the POSH Act before the Industrial Tribunal / High Court; criminal complaint under Section 74/75 BNS.
source_authority: LegalConnect Workplace Rights Directorate

parent_act_name: POSH Act, 2013
title_english: Right to 90 Days Paid Interim Relief & Transfer During Workplace Harassment Inquiry
title_hindi: पॉश जांच के दौरान 90 दिनों के सवैतनिक अंतरिम अवकाश (Paid Leave) और स्थानांतरण का अधिकार
summary_or_content: During the pendency of a workplace harassment inquiry, the aggrieved woman has the statutory right to request up to 3 months of paid leave (in addition to her regular annual leave) or transfer to another branch to prevent intimidation.
confrontation_script_en: HR / ICC, under Section 12 of the POSH Act 2013, I am formally requesting 90 days of paid interim relief leave / department transfer to ensure a safe, non-retaliatory environment during this ongoing inquiry.
confrontation_script_hi: एचआर और आंतरिक समिति, पॉश कानून की धारा 12 के तहत मैं जांच चलने तक 90 दिनों के सवैतनिक अवकाश (Paid Leave) या अन्य विभाग में स्थानांतरण की मांग करती हूँ, ताकि मैं भयमुक्त रह सकूँ।
actionable_dos: Request interim relief in writing with reference to Section 12 of POSH Act.; Ensure the leave is coded as "Statutory Interim POSH Leave", not personal sick leave.; Report any subtle retaliation or hostile cold-shouldering immediately to the ICC.
actionable_donts: Do NOT allow HR to deduct this leave from your earned or casual leave balance.; Do NOT agree to reporting to the accused during the inquiry period.; Do NOT resign under pressure; exercise your statutory rights to interim transfer.
legal_remedy: If the employer refuses, file an urgent application before the District Local Complaints Committee (LCC) or writ before the High Court.
emergency_helpline: Ministry of Women & Child Development SHe-Box: 011-23386423
source_authority: LegalConnect Workplace Rights Directorate

parent_act_name: Information Technology Act, 2000 & IT Intermediary Rules, 2021
section_or_code: Section 66E, Section 67A, Rule 3(2)(b) IT Rules 2021, Section 77 BNS
title_english: Right Against Deepfakes, Morphed Images & Non-Consensual Media
title_hindi: डीपफेक, मॉर्फ्ड फोटो और बिना सहमति की अश्लील सामग्री के खिलाफ 24 घंटे में हटाने का अधिकार
summary_or_content: Publishing, transmitting, or creating morphed images, deepfakes, or intimate media of a person without explicit consent is punishable with up to 5 years imprisonment. Social media intermediaries are legally obligated to remove such content within 24 hours of grievance receipt.
confrontation_script_en: Grievance Officer / Cyber Police, under Rule 3(2)(b) of the Information Technology Rules, 2021 and Section 66E/67A of the IT Act, you are legally mandated to disable access to this non-consensual morphed media within 24 hours of this complaint.
confrontation_script_hi: शिकायत अधिकारी / साइबर सेल, आईटी नियम 2021 के नियम 3(2)(b) और आईटी एक्ट की धारा 66E/67A के तहत बिना सहमति की मॉर्फ्ड/डीपफेक सामग्री को शिकायत के 24 घंटे के भीतर इंटरनेट से हटाना अनिवार्य है।
actionable_dos: Take timestamped screenshots and copy exact URLs before requesting deletion.; Submit the complaint directly to the platform designated Grievance Officer.; Use StopNCII.org to generate an encrypted digital hash of the media to block re-uploads.
actionable_donts: Do NOT pay extortion or blackmail ransom to cyber criminals; they rarely delete media.; Do NOT delete your chat history with the perpetrator; it serves as primary digital evidence.; Do NOT blame yourself; non-consensual morphing is a serious cyber felony.
legal_remedy: Emergency take-down petition before the High Court; complaint before the Grievance Appellate Committee (GAC) at gac.gov.in.
source_authority: LegalConnect Cyber Law Directorate

parent_act_name: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 & Banking Directives
section_or_code: Section 106 BNSS (Old Sec 102 CrPC), Article 300A Constitution
title_english: Right to Contest Bank Account Lien & Cyber Freeze for Innocent P2P Transactions
title_hindi: साइबर पुलिस द्वारा निर्दोष बैंक खाते को फ्रीज (लेन-देन पर रोक) करने के खिलाफ अधिकार
summary_or_content: Police cannot freeze an entire bank account when only a fraction of funds is disputed in a cyber fraud chain. Citizens have the right to demand restriction of the lien only to the disputed amount, leaving remaining balances free for normal living expenses.
confrontation_script_en: Branch Manager & Investigating Officer, under Section 106 of BNSS and High Court precedents, police can only place a debit freeze on the specific disputed amount in question, not my entire account. I demand immediate unfreezing of all undisputed balances for my essential livelihood.
confrontation_script_hi: शाखा प्रबंधक और जांच अधिकारी, बीएनएसएस की धारा 106 और उच्च न्यायालय के निर्देशों के अनुसार आप केवल विवादित राशि पर ही रोक लगा सकते हैं, पूरे खाते को फ्रीज नहीं कर सकते। कृपया मेरे शेष वैध पैसे को तुरंत चालू (Unfreeze) करें।
actionable_dos: Demand the specific Police Notice Number, Station Name, and disputed transaction ID from your bank.; Collect and organize all transaction receipts, chats, and proof of legitimate sale/trade.; Request the bank in writing to limit the debit restriction strictly to the questioned amount.
actionable_donts: Do NOT panic and try to open fraudulent secondary accounts to siphon funds.; Do NOT ignore the freeze; unresolved cyber notices can result in notice under BNSS Sec 94/179.; Do NOT pay unauthorized middle-men claiming to "clear" police cyber complaints.
legal_remedy: Application under Section 497 BNSS before the Magistrate Court; Section 528 BNSS / Article 226 writ before the High Court.
emergency_helpline: National Cyber Financial Fraud Reporting Desk: 1930
source_authority: LegalConnect Cyber & Banking Committee

parent_act_name: Model Tenancy Act & State Rent Control Acts
section_or_code: Section 20 Model Tenancy Act, Section 108 Transfer of Property Act, Section 126 BNS (Wrongful Restraint)
title_english: Absolute Protection Against Landlord Utility Disconnections (Water & Electricity)
title_hindi: मकान मालिक द्वारा बिजली-पानी काटने पर पूर्ण कानूनी रोक का अधिकार
summary_or_content: Landlords are strictly prohibited from severing essential municipal amenities (drinking water, electricity, lift, or parking) to force a tenant to vacate, even during an active rent dispute. The Rent Authority can fine the landlord up to ₹50,000 and restore connections immediately.
confrontation_script_en: Landlord, under Section 20 of the Tenancy Act, cutting off my electricity or water supply is a cognizable legal offense. If not restored within 24 hours, I will file an urgent petition before the Rent Authority for restoration with statutory penalties.
confrontation_script_hi: मकान मालिक, किरायेदारी अधिनियम की धारा 20 के तहत किराए के विवाद में भी बिजली या पानी काटना गैरकानूनी और दंडनीय अपराध है। यदि 24 घंटे में आपूर्ति बहाल नहीं हुई तो मैं किराया प्राधिकरण में क्षतिपूर्ति की याचिका दायर करूँगा।
actionable_dos: Photograph the tampered meter box and document the exact time of disconnection.; Send a formal WhatsApp notice and registered speed post notice immediately.; Continue offering the rent via bank transfer / UPI to prove you are a lawful tenant.
actionable_donts: Do NOT tamper with the high-voltage municipal meter yourself.; Do NOT vacate the house in panic without obtaining a formal court order or legal advice.; Do NOT stop paying basic rent, as it weakens your tenancy locus standi.
legal_remedy: Urgent application before the Rent Authority under Section 20; Section 126 BNS police complaint; civil injunction suit.
emergency_helpline: Department of Housing & Urban Affairs Citizen Desk: 011-23063281
source_authority: LegalConnect Tenancy & Real Estate Council

parent_act_name: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 & Indian Contract Act, 1872
section_or_code: Section 11 Model Tenancy Act, Section 73 Indian Contract Act, 1872
title_english: Mandatory 30-Day Security Deposit Refund & Deduction Safeguards
title_hindi: मकान खाली करने के 30 दिनों में सुरक्षा राशि (Security Deposit) वापसी का अधिकार
summary_or_content: Landlords must refund the security deposit to the tenant within 30 days of vacating the premises. Deductions can only be made for actual documented structural damages beyond normal wear and tear, accompanied by GST repair invoices.
confrontation_script_en: Landlord, under Section 11 of the Tenancy Act, my security deposit must be refunded within 30 days of handover. Deductions cannot be made for normal wear and tear, and you must provide verified GST invoices for any alleged repairs.
confrontation_script_hi: मकान मालिक, किरायेदारी अधिनियम की धारा 11 के तहत मकान खाली करने के 30 दिनों के भीतर पूरी सुरक्षा राशि (Security Deposit) लौटाना अनिवार्य है। सामान्य टूट-फूट पर कटौती नहीं की जा सकती और हर कटौती का पक्का जीएसटी बिल देना होगा।
actionable_dos: Shoot a comprehensive walk-through video of the property right before handing over the keys.; Get the landlord to sign a handover note confirming possession returned in good condition.; Send account bank details in writing for electronic deposit transfer.
actionable_donts: Do NOT surrender all physical keys without an acknowledgement of move-out date.; Do NOT accept arbitrary lump-sum verbal deductions without itemized bills.; Do NOT delay issuing a legal notice if the 30-day timeline lapses.
legal_remedy: Petition before the Rent Authority; Summary recovery suit under Order 37 CPC; Consumer Forum complaint for deficiency in service.
source_authority: LegalConnect Tenancy & Housing Council

parent_act_name: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 & Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023
section_or_code: Article 51A(g) Constitution, Rule 20 ABC Rules 2023, Section 11 PCA Act 1960
title_english: Right to Feed Community Animals & Protection Against RWA Intimidation
title_hindi: बेजुबान जानवरों को खाना खिलाने का संवैधानिक अधिकार और आरडब्ल्यूए उत्पीड़न के खिलाफ सुरक्षा
summary_or_content: Citizens have a constitutional duty and legal right to feed community street dogs in designated areas. Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs) or local societies cannot impose fines, threaten caregivers, or relocate street animals.
confrontation_script_en: RWA Committee, under Article 51A(g) of the Constitution and Rule 20 of the ABC Rules 2023 affirmed by the Supreme Court, caring for and feeding community animals is a protected constitutional right. Imposing illegal fines or intimidating feeders attracts criminal prosecution under the law.
confrontation_script_hi: आरडब्ल्यूए प्रबंधन, संविधान के अनुच्छेद 51A(g) और पशु जन्म नियंत्रण नियम 2023 के तहत बेजुबान जानवरों को खाना खिलाना हर नागरिक का संवैधानिक कर्तव्य है। खाना खिलाने वालों पर जुर्माना लगाना या धमकाना कानूनी अपराध है।
actionable_dos: Feed community dogs in fixed, designated clean spots away from children play areas.; Coordinate with local municipal authorities for ABC (sterilization and anti-rabies vaccination).; Keep copies of the AWBI guidelines and Supreme Court ruling handy.
actionable_donts: Do NOT allow food waste or dirty bowls to litter public walkways.; Do NOT engage in violent verbal shouting matches with aggressive residents; record proof calmly.; Do NOT relocate healthy community dogs outside their natural geographical territory.
legal_remedy: Criminal complaint for criminal intimidation under Section 351 BNS; writ petition before the High Court; complaint to the Animal Welfare Board of India.
source_authority: LegalConnect Civic & Animal Rights Directorate

parent_act_code: DGCA CAR Section 3 Series M Part IV
parent_act_name: Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR)
section_or_code: CAR Section 3, Series M, Part IV, Consumer Protection Act, 2019
title_english: DGCA Passenger Charter: Cash Compensation & Amenities for Delayed or Cancelled Flights
title_hindi: डीजीसीए पैसेंजर चार्टर: फ्लाइट लेट या कैंसिल होने पर मुफ्त भोजन, होटल व नकद मुआवजे का अधिकार
summary_or_content: If a flight is delayed by over 2 hours, airlines must provide free meals and refreshments. For cancellations communicated within 24 hours or delays over 6 hours at night, airlines must provide free hotel accommodation or statutory cash compensation up to ₹10,000–₹20,000.
confrontation_script_en: Airline Duty Manager, under DGCA Passenger Charter CAR Section 3 Series M Part IV, as my flight has been delayed beyond the statutory threshold, you are legally obligated to provide immediate complimentary refreshments/hotel accommodation or alternative routing without surcharge.
confrontation_script_hi: एयरलाइन ड्यूटी मैनेजर, डीजीसीए पैसेंजर चार्टर (CAR Section 3) के अनुसार, मेरी उड़ान निर्धारित समय से अधिक लेट हो चुकी है। आप नियमानुसार मुफ्त भोजन, जलपान और होटल आवास या मुआवजा प्रदान करने के लिए बाध्य हैं।
actionable_dos: Preserve your physical or digital boarding pass and all airport departure screen photos.; Obtain a written delay certificate or stamp from the airline ground supervisor.; File your AirSewa grievance within 30 days of the travel date.
actionable_donts: Do NOT accept arbitrary airline blame citing "ATC delay" when other flights are departing normally.; Do NOT leave the airport without demanding your statutory meal or accommodation vouchers.; Do NOT accept airline credit vouchers with restrictive short expiry dates if you prefer a cash bank refund.
legal_remedy: Complaint before the DGCA AirSewa Portal; District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
source_authority: LegalConnect Aviation & Passenger Charter Council

parent_act_name: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
title_english: Elderly Parents Right to Revoke Property Gift Deeds for Neglect or Abandonment
title_hindi: वरिष्ठ नागरिक माता-पिता द्वारा उपेक्षा पर बच्चों को दी गई संपत्ति की रजिस्ट्री रद्द कराने का अधिकार
summary_or_content: If an elderly parent transfers property to their children on the condition that they provide basic physical amenities, and the children neglect them, the Maintenance Tribunal has statutory power under Section 23 to declare the transfer deed void as fraudulent.
confrontation_script_en: Under Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, any property transferred to children becomes void if they fail to provide medical care, food, and emotional support. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate Tribunal will cancel the deed and restore possession.
confrontation_script_hi: माता-पिता और वरिष्ठ नागरिक भरण-पोषण अधिनियम 2007 की धारा 23 के तहत, यदि संतान माता-पिता की देखभाल और दवा का ध्यान नहीं रखती, तो एसडीएम ट्रिब्यूनल गिफ्ट की गई संपत्ति की रजिस्ट्री को रद्द कर संपत्ति वापस दिला सकता है।
actionable_dos: Keep copies of the original sale deed, gift deed, and medical treatment expense receipts.; Approach the local SDM (Sub-Divisional Magistrate) office directly or dial 14567 for free government aid.; Seek an interim order preventing the children from selling or creating third-party rights on the property.
actionable_donts: Do NOT feel helpless or accept physical/verbal abuse in your own home.; Do NOT get bogged down in endless civil court suits; the Senior Citizens Tribunal is specifically fast-tracked.; Do NOT sign power of attorney papers or blank papers under emotional duress.
legal_remedy: Application before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Maintenance Tribunal; appeal before the District Magistrate (Appellate Tribunal).
source_authority: LegalConnect Senior Citizens Welfare Council
